frames.narration: Query: user_id, country, amount for the last 7 days where amount >= 900. The table has 30 days (about 994 MB as row files, or 12 million rows of 138 bytes), partitioned by day.
Partition pruning: only the 7 newest day folders match the filter. The other 23 are dropped from the path alone, with no file opened. That is 14 files left (2 per day), about 23% of the data.
The engine reads each remaining file's footer with a small ranged read: schema and min/max per column per row group. 14 files, 8 row groups each, 56 row groups in all.
Row group skipping: data is sorted by amount inside each day, so a group whose max amount is 624 cannot match amount >= 900. 49 of 56 groups are ruled out from the stats alone; 7 remain.
Column pruning: of the 5 columns, the engine needs user_id, country and amount. The 120-byte payload chunk is never fetched.
The chunks come back dictionary-encoded and compressed. The engine decodes them and keeps the rows with amount >= 900.
Result: about 3.8 MB read, 0.4% of the 994 MB table. Without sorting, stats could skip nothing and it reads 28 MB (2.8%); as row files it reads 232 MB (23%) even with partitioning.
